vocab.en: Are you ready to order? (lit. "Have you chosen?")

vocab.notes: Usually sliced bread dumplings, served with goulash and sauces.
A Czech classic: breaded fried cheese, usually with chips and tartare sauce (tatarka).
Always plural. s hranolky = with chips.
Plural of brambor. s brambory = with potatoes.
Two to four set dishes at lunchtime (usually about 11:00–14:00), often with soup, at a good price.

dialogue.setting: Lunch with a colleague at a traditional pub near the office. Like most places near offices, it has a daily lunch menu.

lines.speaker: Číšnice
lines.en: Hello, are you ready to order?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.cs: Ano. Chtěla bych gulášovou [[polévku|polévka|acc|object]] a smažený sýr.
lines.en: Yes. I'd like the goulash soup and the fried cheese.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.cs: Já bych si dal [[řízek|řízek|acc|object]] s bramborovým [[salátem|salát|ins|with-s]].
lines.en: I'd have the schnitzel with potato salad.

lines.speaker: Číšnice
lines.en: I'm afraid we've run out of schnitzel.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Then the goulash with dumplings, please.

exercises.en: I'd like the goulash. (a man speaking)
exercises.why: Polite requests use the conditional: chtěl bych (man) / chtěla bych (woman), literally "I would want".

hints.explain: With bych you need the past form (the l-participle): chtěl bych, not chci bych.
chtěla is what a woman says. Here a man is speaking: chtěl.

exercises.why: In the accusative, feminine adjectives change -á to -ou: zeleninová polévka → zeleninovou polévku.

hints.explain: The adjective must agree with polévku (accusative), so zeleninová → zeleninovou.
Close: nouns take -u, but feminine adjectives take -ou in the accusative: zeleninovou polévku.

exercises.why: Máte…? (Do you have…?) is how to ask what's available. guláš is masculine inanimate, so it doesn't change in the accusative.

hints.explain: Máš is the ty form. In a restaurant, use vy: Máte guláš?

exercises.prompt: I'd like a schnitzel, please. (a woman speaking)
answers: {Chtěla bych|Dala bych si|Dám si} řízek[, prosím].
exercises.why: A woman says chtěla bych or dala bych si. řízek is masculine inanimate and doesn't change.

hints.explain: The l-form agrees with the speaker. A woman says chtěla bych / dala bych si.

exercises.question: Which case is "knedlíkem"?
exercises.why: s (with) takes the instrumental. Masculine nouns take -em: knedlík → s knedlíkem.

exercises.prompt: Say (as a man) that you'd like the fried cheese with chips.
answers: [Ano[,] ]{Chtěl bych|Dal bych si|Dám si} smažený sýr s hranolky[, prosím].
exercises.why: Order with Chtěl bych / Dal bych si / Dám si + accusative. smažený sýr is masculine inanimate, so it doesn't change. "With chips" is s hranolky.

hints.wrong: [Ano[,] ]{Chtěl bych|Dal bych si|Dám si} smažený sýr s hranolkami[, prosím].
hints.explain: hranolky is masculine, so its instrumental plural stays hranolky: s hranolky. -ami is a feminine ending.

hints.wrong: [Ano[,] ]{Chtěla bych|Dala bych si} smažený sýr s hranolky[, prosím].
hints.explain: You're a man here: chtěl bych / dal bych si.

answers: {Unfortunately|Sorry|I'm afraid}[,] we {don't have|have no} {schnitzel|schnitzels|the schnitzel|any schnitzel} {anymore|any more|left}[.]
We don't have {schnitzel|any schnitzel|the schnitzel} {anymore|any more|left}[,] unfortunately[.]
{Unfortunately|Sorry|I'm afraid}[,] we{'ve run| have run|'re| are} out of {schnitzel|schnitzels}[.]
exercises.why: už + a negative verb means "not any more"; bohužel means "unfortunately".
pro (for) takes the accusative. Masculine animate nouns (people and animals) add -a: pán → pro pána.

hints.explain: -u is the accusative of feminine nouns in -a (kávu). pán is masculine animate, and adds -a: pro pána.
